faq.a: Djibril is associated with the Arabic form جِبْرِيل, whose core sense is djibril; gabriel (angel) (west african form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Djibril?
faq.a: Djibril is associated with Arabic. Djibril is the West African form of Arabic جِبْرِيل (Jibrīl), the Quranic name of the angel Gabriel.
Yes — the underlying form جِبْرِيل is Arabic.
Djibril can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Djibril should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Jibrīl is the Quranic Arabic name of the angel Gabriel and occurs in the Quran.

faq.q: What does Djibril mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Djibril is rendered جبریل and carries the sense جبریل، فرشتہ.

faq.q: What does Djibril mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Djibril is rendered جبرئیل and carries the sense جبرئیل، فرشته.
A romanized syllable approximation is djib-ril. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Djibril?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Djibril, djibril. Script forms are جبرئیل, جبرائيل, جبریل, جِبْرِيل, जिब्रील.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
